_why: The plan is evidence only if it demonstrably predates the outcome. Commit dates can be set to anything; GitHub's merge timestamp cannot. This file records that timestamp and binds it to the exact bytes of the plan that was merged. It is written SEPARATELY so that T4.plan.json stays byte-identical to what was frozen — the plan is never edited after its freeze, not even to fill in its own metadata.
verifyIndependently: The merge time is served by GitHub's own API for PR 133 and cannot be rewritten by this repository.
sha256 of the plan file at the merge commit must equal planSha256 above. Checked at 17:35Z: the merge commit's copy and the working copy hash identically.
reconcile.ts asserts this timestamp precedes the first register's block time, and marks the pool UNFROZEN if it does not.

poolAtFreeze.note: Unlike T1, T4's pool already existed at the freeze and is named in the plan: pool 15. It held zero entrants when the plan was merged. That is read rather than assumed — the indexer reported pool 15 Open at 0/64 at 16:18Z, four minutes BEFORE the merge, and again at 17:34Z, seventy-two minutes after it. Nothing entered in between, so it was 0 at 16:22:00Z.
